title: Windows: the daemon cannot install signal handlers, and warns about a mode Windows does not have
description: Two Windows-only defects found the first time the desktop integration tests ran on a Windows runner. (1) cli._install_signal_handlers calls loop.add_signal_handler, which asyncio's Windows loops raise NotImplementedError from -- so the bundled daemon died during startup and all three integration tests failed with 'no port file'. (2) secrets.load warns that gateway.env is 'readable by other accounts (mode 666); run chmod 600', which on Windows is always wrong: the POSIX mode is synthetic there and chmod is not a program the machine has.
close_reason: Signals install through whichever mechanism the platform has; the mode warning is POSIX-only. tests/test_signals.py and a new case in test_secrets.py cover both, verified failing without the fix.

title: Windows build: CreateJobObjectW missing without the Win32_Security feature
description: windows-sys gates individual functions on every feature their signature reaches into, not just the module. CreateJobObjectW takes a *const SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES, so with Win32_System_JobObjects enabled but Win32_Security not, the symbol simply is not there and rustc reports it as an unresolved import with a 'did you mean CreateJobSet' suggestion. Windows-only; macOS and Linux never compile supervisor.rs's job module.
close_reason: Win32_Security added to the windows-sys feature list

title: Windows tauri-build fails: icons/icon.ico missing
description: tauri-build generates a Windows Resource file at compile time and needs an .ico from bundle.icon; the icons directory shipped only PNGs, so every Windows leg of the desktop workflow failed with 'icons/icon.ico not found'. macOS and Linux never look for it. Generate the missing icon.ico (and icon.icns, the other half of Tauri's default icon list) from the existing placeholder icon.png.
close_reason: icon.ico and icon.icns generated from icon.png with cargo tauri icon and committed

title: Desktop workflow does not watch scripts/bundle_python.py
description: The Desktop shell workflow runs 'make tauri-python', which is scripts/bundle_python.py, but that path is absent from both push and pull_request path filters. The Windows uv-alias fix (4099647) therefore merged without the workflow that would have proved it ever running -- the only Windows evidence on record is run #2 on the pre-fix commit 93ce144. Add the script to both copies of the path list.
close_reason: Both path lists now watch scripts/bundle_python.py

title: UI: prompt and tool forms render no send button (dataset assignment throws)
description: schema_form.js has its own el() helper that lacks the 'dataset' branch app.js's el() has. It falls through to `k in node` -> `node.dataset = {...}`, and dataset is a readonly WebIDL attribute, so in a module (strict mode) the assignment throws TypeError. renderField() and buildPromptForm() both pass dataset, so buildForm/buildPromptForm throw, renderToolDetail/renderPromptDetail abort, and the detail panel shows the heading with no form and no send button. Templates are unaffected (they use app.js's el).
acceptance_criteria: Opening a prompt (e.g. zoo-prompt-animal) or a tool with fields shows its form and its send button; data-field is set on each field so the variables column can fill it.
close_reason: el() in schema_form.js and render.js now handle dataset explicitly

title: A backend restart never told clients the catalogue changed
description: Gateway.restart_backend invalidates the catalogue but emits no list_changed, so a UI open across a restart keeps showing the old tools, prompts and resources until someone presses Refresh. reload() and a backend's own notification both announce; the restart path was the one that did not.
close_reason: restart_backend now emits one list_changed per kind through the debounced notifier; regression test in test_notifications.py, verified failing without the fix.

title: Three UI bugs only a browser found: painted gate, /ui base URL, endless retry
description: Found by driving the page in headless Chromium over CDP. (1) .gate sets display:grid, which outranks the UA stylesheet's [hidden]{display:none}, so the access-key overlay was painted permanently over a working page while el.hidden reported true -- every DOM assertion passed. Fixed with an explicit [hidden]{display:none!important}. (2) A document served at /ui has / as its base URL, so the browser resolved style.css to /style.css and 404'd: an unstyled page with no JS from a URL that answered 200. /ui now 308s to /ui/, preserving the query string. (3) A page on the gate reconnected forever, a 401 every few seconds; a socket that never connected now stops after three attempts.
acceptance_criteria: Gate is display:none when hidden; /ui 308s to /ui/ keeping ?key=; retries bounded. tests/test_webui.py covers the redirect.
close_reason: Closed

title: make run never started the daemon: cli.py had no __main__ guard
description: scripts/start-gateway.sh invokes 'python -m mcp_gateway.cli'. cli.py defined run() but had no 'if __name__ == "__main__"' guard, so the module imported, defined everything and exited 0 without binding anything. The Makefile prints the banner itself, so it looked exactly like a daemon that had started. The console script (mcp-gateway) calls run() through its entry point and was never affected, which is why every test and every hand-run missed it. Found while verifying 'make run-dev'.
acceptance_criteria: 'python -m mcp_gateway.cli --check' runs and exits 0 with the check report; tests/test_cli_paths.py asserts it.
close_reason: Closed

title: Phase 5: tools fan-out (MVP)
description: supervisor.py eager sweep + readiness event, catalogue.py (tools), router.py (tools/call).
acceptance_criteria: test_startup, test_aggregation, test_tools_call, test_dead_backend pass; usable from Claude Code
close_reason: supervisor.py (eager concurrent sweep, readiness event, required-backend refusal), catalogue.py (per-backend cache, list_changed invalidation, skipped-name recording), router.py (the per-method dead-backend policy). Wired into gateway.py. 260 tests green. Verified live: 3 backends configured, 2 running, 1 skipped with a readable reason; namespaced tools routed correctly through the real bridge; no secret in the log. Found: the gateway must not declare client capabilities before the passthrough handler exists — MCPStdioClient's conformance guard refuses a promise with nothing behind it.

title: Phase 3: WS daemon, zero backends
description: jsonrpc.py, transport_ws.py (lifted, de-ACP'd, path routing /mcp vs /admin), session.py, minimal gateway.py, admin.py (list_backends), tests/fixtures/ws_client.py.
acceptance_criteria: test_ws_auth, test_ws_lifecycle, test_capabilities, test_admin_tools pass
close_reason: jsonrpc.py, transport_ws.py (lifted, de-ACP'd, /mcp + /admin path routing, Bearer accepted), session.py, gateway.py composition root, admin.py with the four meta-tools, tests/fixtures/ws_client.py. title: Phase 4: mcp-gateway-connect stdio bridge
description: bridge.py stdin<->WS pump, second console entrypoint, make connect target, claude mcp add line in banner. Reconnect with backoff.
acceptance_criteria: test_bridge passes; stdout purity verified
close_reason: bridge.py + mcp-gateway-connect entrypoint. 14 tests incl. stdout purity, parse-error handling, EOF exit, and survive-a-daemon-restart. Two real bugs found by the tests: the stdin pump raced ahead of the first connection (a client writes initialize the instant it spawns the bridge), and _ClientHungUp was raised in a task nobody awaited so EOF hung instead of exiting. Also: only requests actually sent are failed on a drop, so a queued one survives a reconnect. 219 tests green.

title: Phase 2: backend MCP stdio client
description: Lift mcp_stdio.py+md from python-acp with env_replace/clientInfo/protocol-constants adaptations; protocol.py; backend.py; tests/fixtures/mock_backend.py.

title: MCP Gateway daemon (epic)
description: WebSocket MCP gateway daemon with consolidated credential store in gateway.env, fanning out to stdio backend MCP subprocesses. Plan: ~/.claude/plans/i-want-a-mcp-snoopy-tulip.md

title: Clipboard payloads are encoded as TOON
description: The briefing's request/response fences were pretty-printed JSON, which spends most of its lines on punctuation the reading model pays for. Added src/mcp_gateway/toon.py (encoder only, spec-conformant for the shapes a briefing holds) and pointed clipboard._fence at it.

title: Clipboard modal: preview toggle for the rendered Markdown
description: The Clipboard modal shows the briefing as plain text in a textarea. The document is Markdown (rendered by clipboard.py), so a person trimming it before pasting has no way to see what it looks like rendered. Add a Preview toggle beside Regenerate that swaps the textarea for a rendered view, with a local escaping-only Markdown renderer (no HTML passthrough: the document quotes untrusted backend output).
close_reason: Preview toggle shipped: ui/markdown.js renderer, toggle in the Clipboard modal, styles, docs, CHANGELOG, and two test suites.

title: Write GET_STARTED.md and refresh docs that should point at it
description: New users have README (a pitch + reference) and per-module .md files (reasoning), but no single walkthrough: install, configure a backend, attach a client, use the admin UI, and -- the part nothing user-facing covers -- how to publish resources/templates from your own MCP server so the Injectable values column activates. Add GET_STARTED.md and link it from README, ARCHITECTURE, desktop/README and examples.
close_reason: GET_STARTED.md written; README, ARCHITECTURE, webui.md, desktop/README, servers.dev.yaml, gateway.env.example, CHANGELOG, CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md updated. make lint / docs-check / test all green.

title: Idle-sweep tests assume time.monotonic() is large
description: tests/test_idle_backends.py backdated last_call_monotonic to an absolute 0.0 and expected a 3600s idle_ttl to have elapsed. time.monotonic() counts from boot on Linux, so on a GitHub runner two minutes old that means 'idle for 120s' and the sweep correctly does nothing. Two tests failed in CI and passed on a developer Mac that had been up nine days. Backend.idle_for documents this exact hazard in its own source.
acceptance_criteria: The idle tests backdate relative to time.monotonic() and pass on a freshly booted machine.
close_reason: Backdating is now relative to time.monotonic() via idle_since_long_ago(), and IDLE_TTL is named once so the helper can be sure it clears it. Demonstrated: with a simulated fresh-boot clock (monotonic=120s) the old absolute 0.0 yields idle_for=120 and no sweep; the relative backdate yields 7200 and sweeps, on any clock.

title: Clipboard: an agent-ready briefing of the Results and Injectable values columns
description: The admin UI can show a person what a backend answered, but there is no way to hand that session to an agent. Add a 'Clipboard' button to the Results column that opens a modal holding a generated text document -- every result card and every injectable value -- editable in place, with a Copy button. Render the document in Python so the same text is available over MCP: a gateway__clipboard meta-tool and admin.clipboard.* on /admin, one implementation, two surfaces (admin.md's existing pattern). The UI publishes its column state to the gateway; the tool renders the last published snapshot.
design: New module clipboard.py holds the Workbench (latest snapshot, process-wide) and render(). gateway.py owns one. admin.py gets the tool definition and the two /admin methods. ui/clipboard.js holds the modal. The UI posts a snapshot on every change, debounced.
acceptance_criteria: Button in the centre column opens a modal with an editable textarea and a working Copy; gateway__clipboard appears in tools/list and returns the same text; admin.clipboard.get returns it too; pytest and tests/ui suites cover both.
close_reason: Clipboard button, modal editor and gateway__clipboard landed; 606 pytest + 123 jsdom green.

title: Full primitive descriptions as a hover tooltip in the left column
description: A primitive row ellipsizes its description to one line, which for most servers is the first few words of a paragraph. The full text is only in the detail pane, behind a click -- too far to help someone deciding which row to click. Show it as a tooltip on hover and on focus.
acceptance_criteria: Hovering or focusing a primitive row shows its full description in a positioned tooltip; the tooltip is clamped to the window and flips above the row near the bottom edge; rows with no description show nothing; jsdom coverage.
close_reason: A singleton #tooltip in index.html, position: fixed and placed by placeTooltip (below the row, clamped to the window, flipped above near the bottom edge) -- the same arrangement as placeMenu, because the column's overflow-y clips anything inside it. 250ms on hover, immediate on focus, aria-describedby while shown, dismissed on blur/Escape/scroll/resize/click and on every renderPrimitives rebuild. pointer-events: none stops the hover-flicker loop. tests/ui/tooltip.test.mjs, 10 cases. 590 pytest, 108 jsdom, lint and docs-check green.

title: Results append below and autoscroll; right column reads 'Injectable values'
description: Two UI changes. The Results column prepended, so a new card landed above the one just read and the reading order fought the invocation order; it should append and scroll the new card into view. The right column's header said 'Variables', which names the mechanism rather than what the column is for -- it holds the values that can be injected into a form.
acceptance_criteria: New result cards appear at the bottom and the column scrolls to show them; the right column's heading and accessible name both read 'Injectable values'; jsdom suite updated and green.
close_reason: Results cards append and the column scrolls to the bottom; the right column's heading, its region aria-label and the gutter label all read 'Injectable values'. Class names and ids stay 'variables' -- the code's word for the mechanism, not the column's word for its purpose. results.test.mjs updated for the new order plus a scroll assertion. 590 pytest, 98 jsdom, lint and docs-check green.

title: Results cards get a per-card delete button
description: The Results column can only be cleared wholesale via the Clear button. Add a trashcan-icon delete to each result card's meta row so one card can be dismissed without losing the rest, restoring the empty state when the last one goes.
acceptance_criteria: Every result card carries a trashcan button; clicking it removes that card only; removing the last card restores the empty-state paragraph; covered by a jsdom test.
close_reason: Each result card now carries a trashcan button in its meta row, beside Copy JSON: an inline SVG built through createElementNS, styled with the existing .ghost.danger hover. The card removes itself and calls onRemove; pushCard uses that to restore the empty-state paragraph when the last card goes, and clearResults is now the one definition the Clear button shares. tests/ui/results.test.mjs covers isolation, the icon's namespace, the empty-state restore and the push-after-empty path. 590 pytest, 97 jsdom, lint and docs-check green.

title: Splash the desktop launch instead of accusing the access key
description: The window painted 'This gateway may require an access key' during the ordinary startup window, then connected. Cause: the shell's first gw_open answers 'not listening yet' while a cold interpreter imports, the socket closes, and the closed handler wrote the key message. Fixed with ranked gate modes (connecting/blocked/failed) so a socket close cannot outrank the host's own state.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lay the server editor out in three columns
description: The server editor dialog was a single 34rem column of ten fields, which scrolled. Group the spec into Process / Environment / Behaviour and lay the three side by side so the whole thing is visible at once.
close_reason: Closed

title: Sign and notarise the desktop bundle, and give it a real icon
description:
The .app is unsigned, un-notarised, and wears a generated placeholder icon (scripts that made it are inline in the commit; there is no design).

Signing a bundled interpreter is the part that surprises people: every nested Mach-O under Contents/Resources/python needs signing with the hardened runtime, and a standalone CPython typically needs com.apple.security.cs.allow-unsigned-executable-memory for ctypes. Budget a day.

Also bring back the dmg bundle target, dropped in python-mcp-gateway-af1 because bundle_dmg.sh drives Finder through AppleScript and cannot run unattended. It belongs with this work.
acceptance_criteria: A notarised .app and .dmg that open on a machine that has never seen the developer's certificate, with no Gatekeeper prompt beyond the first-open dialog.

title: First-run app data, Makefile targets and docs for the desktop shell
description:
Seed servers.yaml (everything disabled, so a first launch starts nothing and fails nothing) and gateway.env (mode 0600, WS_ACCESS_KEY line removed since the env var always wins under Tauri) into the Tauri app config dir. --env needs nothing: cli.default_env_path already resolves gateway.env beside the resolved config.

Plus: make tauri-deps/tauri-dev/tauri-bundle, .gitignore entries, distclean (not clean -- both trees need the network to rebuild, same reasoning as .venv), desktop/README.md carrying the why, and ARCHITECTURE.md/README.md updates.
acceptance_criteria: A first launch on a machine with no app data dir comes up clean; make docs-check passes; clean leaves the resources and target trees alone and distclean removes them.
close_reason: Proxy, shim and app wiring landed. Rust opens /mcp and /admin with Authorization: Bearer and relays opaque frames over a per-connection Tauri Channel; tauri-transport.js swaps rpc.js's transport and is inert in a browser; app.js stands its key/gate handling down under the shell and renders the host's gateway-state instead. First-run seeding, Makefile targets (tauri-python/stage/dev/bundle/check), .gitignore, check_docs target skip, desktop/README.md, ARCHITECTURE/README/CHANGELOG and three module docs. transport_ws.py unmodified.

title: Rust WebSocket proxy over Tauri IPC, and the tauri-transport.js shim
description:
gw_open/gw_send/gw_close plus a per-connection Tauri Channel. Rust opens ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/admin and /mcp with a real Authorization: Bearer header via tokio-tungstenite, and relays frames as opaque strings -- it parses no JSON-RPC and knows nothing about MCP, because the value of the UI's middle column is that what it exercises is byte-identical to what the model gets.

tokio-tungstenite sends no Origin header and origin_permitted() returns True for a None origin, so transport_ws.py needs no change at all. That is the point of this design over letting the webview dial out.

tauri-transport.js is inert in a browser (checks window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__) and ships in webui.ASSETS so one copy of the UI serves both hosts.
acceptance_criteria: All three UI columns populate in the Tauri window with no key prompt; the key appears in the child's environment and nowhere in argv, on disk, or in any IPC payload; transport_ws.py is unmodified; killing the child with the window open turns the pills red then green and re-lists without a page reload.
close_reason: Proxy, shim and app wiring landed. Rust opens /mcp and /admin with Authorization: Bearer and relays opaque frames over a per-connection Tauri Channel; tauri-transport.js swaps rpc.js's transport and is inert in a browser; app.js stands its key/gate handling down under the shell and renders the host's gateway-state instead. First-run seeding, Makefile targets (tauri-python/stage/dev/bundle/check), .gitignore, check_docs target skip, desktop/README.md, ARCHITECTURE/README/CHANGELOG and three module docs. transport_ws.py unmodified.

title: Rust supervisor: spawn, discover the port, restart, kill on exit
description:
Spawn the bundled interpreter as `-m mcp_gateway.cli --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0 --config <appdata>/servers.yaml` with MCP_GATEWAY_WS_KEY and a repaired PATH in the environment, stdout inherited and stderr piped.

--port 0 already works and transport_ws.py:455 already logs 'listening on ws://host:port/mcp' after the backends are up, so that one line is both the readiness signal and the port discovery with no new Python API. Binding an ephemeral port in Rust and passing --port N was rejected: a TOCTOU race for no gain.

Includes the login-shell PATH repair, without which every npx backend fails to spawn in a Finder-launched .app.
acceptance_criteria: A window showing only the child's log proves the child starts, is reachable on the discovered port, restarts with backoff and a floor after repeated immediate failure, and dies on app exit leaving no orphan (pgrep -f mcp_gateway is silent). cargo test covers the stderr parser, the backoff schedule and the PATH parse.
close_reason: Rust crate scaffolded; key.rs, pathenv.rs, supervisor.rs, appdata.rs, proxy.rs and the app wiring in lib.rs. 40 cargo tests, clippy and fmt clean. Port discovered from the daemter's own 'listening on ws://' stderr line; setpgid+killpg+pidfile for orphans; login-shell PATH repair.

title: Pluggable transport seam in rpc.js
description:
rpc.js calls `new WebSocket(this.url())` directly in connect() and reads this.ws.readyState in send(). Make *opening* pluggable via a module-level openTransport + setTransport(), leaving reconnect, backoff, pending bookkeeping and the MCP handshake untouched.

This is worth doing on its own merits, independent of Tauri: tests/ui/harness.mjs currently stubs globalThis.WebSocket with a SilentWebSocket that connects and then does nothing, because that is the only way in. A real seam lets the jsdom suite drive AdminSocket/McpSocket through frames in both directions.
acceptance_criteria: setTransport() exported from rpc.js; the browser path is byte-identical in behaviour; tests/ui/transport.test.mjs covers open, frame in, frame out, close, reconnect backoff and the MCP initialize -> notifications/initialized handshake; make test and make lint pass.
close_reason: setTransport() seam landed in rpc.js; harness switched off the globalThis.WebSocket stub; tests/ui/transport.test.mjs adds 19 tests. 66 JS + 438 pytest green, existing suites unmodified.

title: bundle_python.py: standalone CPython + wheel as Tauri resources
description:
Fetch a relocatable python-build-standalone interpreter for the host triple, install the project wheel and its two pure-Python pinned deps into it, strip what a daemon does not need, and verify the result runs.

Works here because both runtime deps are pure-Python by deliberate choice, so site-packages is architecture-independent and the interpreter is the only per-target artifact.

Sandbox note: pip needs PIP_TRUSTED_HOST="pypi.org files.pythonhosted.org".
acceptance_criteria: make tauri-deps produces desktop/src-tauri/resources/python/ whose interpreter passes both `-c 'import mcp_gateway, websockets, ruamel.yaml'` and `-m mcp_gateway.cli --check`; the build fails loudly if either does; test/idlelib/tkinter/ensurepip are stripped.
close_reason: scripts/bundle_python.py builds a 58MB standalone CPython 3.13.15 with the gateway installed; verified imports, UI assets via importlib.resources, --version and --check. Proven relocatable: a copy at another path binds --port 0 and serves. 35 tests in tests/test_bundle_python.py, 18 in tests/test_desktop_contract.py pinning the stderr line, Bearer-without-Origin, env-beats-file and the seed config.

title: Tauri desktop shell: bundle the gateway and its UI as one app
description:
Ship a Tauri app that owns both halves of the gateway: a Rust host that generates the access key, spawns a bundled-CPython gateway child, and proxies the /admin and /mcp JSON-RPC sockets to an embedded webview running the existing UI assets.

The key is minted in Rust, handed to Python via MCP_GATEWAY_WS_KEY in the environment, and never reaches JavaScript or disk. Because Rust opens the sockets with a real Authorization: Bearer header, the browser-only ?key= carrier stops being load-bearing -- which is what python-mcp-gateway-isb is deferred on.

First cut is a working macOS dev bundle. Cross-platform CI, signing/notarisation and auto-update are separate.

Plan: ~/.claude/plans/lets-add-a-tauri-hidden-pnueli.md
acceptance_criteria: A double-clickable .app on macOS that starts the gateway, populates all three UI columns, prompts for no key, spawns an npx backend when launched from Finder, and leaves no orphan process when quit.
close_reason: Shell landed: make tauri-bundle produces a 96MB MCP Gateway.app. Key minted in Rust per launch, into the child's environment only; both sockets opened by the host with Authorization: Bearer. transport_ws.py unmodified. 504 pytest + 76 node + 43 cargo green, clippy/fmt/lint/docs-check clean. Windowed launch unverified in this environment (no GUI session) -- filed as its own bead.

title: A vocabulary value cannot be put in an enum-constrained field
description:
Found by the new jsdom harness (python-mcp-gateway-6cm), which is the first thing able to reach it.

An enum select built by schema_form.js carries the choice's *index* as each option's value -- deliberately, so `{"enum": [0, 1, 3, 5]}` comes back as the number 3 rather than the string "3" (schema_form.js:355). `putValue` in app.js matches the value it is given against `option.value`, so for any such field the match is index-against-value and always fails: clicking 'asia' in the variables column reports 'asia is not one of the choices this field offers', about a field that offers exactly that.

Reachable whenever a tool or prompt argument has an `enum` in its schema and the same server publishes a vocabulary for that argument's name -- which is the ordinary case for a server that constrains its inputs.
acceptance_criteria: A pick lands in an enum select whose schema names it, the collected value keeps its JSON type (a number stays a number), and a value the field genuinely does not offer still reports so. Covered in tests/ui/.
close_reason: putValue now matches an option on either spelling; schema_form.js carries the choice's own value on option.dataset.value beside the index that collect() needs. Covered in tests/ui/choices.test.mjs.

title: Decide whether the UI JS gets a real test harness (jsdom)
description:
The six files under src/mcp_gateway/ui/ are covered by `node --check` and nothing else.
webui.md and tests/test_webui.py state that position deliberately: "this project has no
Node toolchain and is not acquiring one to run a parser", and what the modules *do* is
verified by eye through `make run-dev`. This issue exists to decide whether the cascade
work changed that calculation, not to assume it did.

The evidence that it might. Two bugs reached a commit in one sitting, both in code no
Python test can reach:

  1. A cascade child inherited its parent's variable, so the grandchild's URI was built by
     writing the country into the continent's segment -- `zoo://continents/congo/countries//animals`.
     Caught before committing, by running the resolver's real source against stub state.
  2. Opening a template after making the picks left every field empty: the column applied
     only `many` picks when a form opened, which was correct until the cascade made
     picking-before-opening the normal order. This one SHIPPED, in 4c8d117, and was found
     by the user in the browser.

Both were logic, not syntax, and both were cheap to catch once there was a DOM to run
against -- jsdom happened to resolve from a global install on this machine, and the fill
path (renderResourceDetail -> applyPicks -> controlFor -> putValue) ran in about thirty
lines of harness.
design:
The shape that fits what already exists, if this is adopted:

- A dev-only dependency. jsdom, in an optional extra or a tests/ui/package.json, NOT a
  runtime one -- the daemon still ships with no Node anything, and the CSP argument in
  webui.md is untouched.
- Driven from pytest, the way tests/test_webui.py::test_the_modules_parse already drives
  `node --check`: skipped when node or jsdom is absent, so a checkout without them stays
  green. That keeps one test command and avoids a second CI toolchain.
- Worth covering, in order of what has actually broken: the variables column's resolver
  (root pairing and dedupe, narrows expansion, pending groups, pick pruning when an
  upstream changes or a vocabulary closes) and the fill path in both directions (a pick
  clicked into an open form, and a form opened onto picks already made).
- Not worth covering: rendering detail, styling, the sockets. The value is in the pure-ish
  logic that the DOM merely hosts.

The honest cost, which is the reason this is a decision and not a task: it reverses a
stated position, adds a second language's dependency to a repo that has none, and jsdom is
not a browser -- it has no layout, so `scrollIntoView` had to be polyfilled even in the
throwaway harness. A test that passes there can still be wrong in a browser.

The alternative is to leave it as it is and accept that UI regressions are found by eye.
That is defensible for a test bench whose whole job is to be looked at; it is less
defensible now that the column has state -- opened sets, chains, picks with lifetimes --
rather than being a renderer of listings.

If declined: webui.md says why, so the next person does not reopen it.

title: Cross-platform desktop bundles (Linux, Windows)
description:
python-mcp-gateway-af1 is macOS and host-architecture only. The Python side is nearly free -- both runtime deps are pure Python, so only the interpreter is per-target and bundle_python.py already maps the uv triple for linux-gnu.

The Rust side is not free:
- Windows has no setpgid/killpg. Orphan control wants a Job Object instead.
- Linux gets PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, which is strictly better than all three layers macOS needs.
- pathenv's login-shell probe is a Unix idea; Windows takes PATH from the registry and a GUI process gets the same one a console process does, so it should no-op (it already does).

Needs its own macOS/Linux/Windows workflow; do not add Rust to the Python test matrix.
acceptance_criteria: publish-artifacts.yml produces a bundle per platform, and tauri-check passes on each.
notes:
Implemented, macOS-verified, CI-unverified on Linux/Windows.

Rust: supervisor.rs grows a Linux PR_SET_PDEATHSIG (SIGTERM, with a getppid re-check for the fork race) and a Windows Job Object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE -- which is the group kill and the pidfile layer in one, so appdata::reap_previous is a documented no-op there. Two portability bugs found on the way: ps -o comm= returns a truncated NAME on Linux where it returns a path on macOS (is_ours now reads /proc/<pid>/exe there, and the reaper would otherwise have been silently off), and platform.machine() says AMD64 on Windows, which no triple in the repo knew.

Python: bundle_python.py gets interpreter_path/stdlib_path and two strip lists (Unix bin/python3 + lib/python3.13, Windows python.exe + Lib + DLLs); both lists are asserted on every platform. New scripts/collect_desktop_bundle.py + 'make tauri-artifacts' names each bundle for its platform and tars the .app (a release cannot hold a directory).

Workflows: .github/workflows/desktop.yml runs 'make tauri-check' on macOS/Linux/Windows per push (ci.yml stays Python-only, per the bead); publish-artifacts.yml gains a 'desktop' job on macos-14, macos-13, ubuntu-22.04 and windows-latest that checks, bundles and uploads. tauri-check now stages the UI when nothing is staged -- generate_context! fails to compile without frontendDist, so it could never have run on a fresh checkout.

What is NOT verified: the Linux and Windows code has never been compiled. rustup could not add a cross target in this sandbox, and cargo check for linux-gnu needs pkg-config for webkit2gtk anyway. The first run of desktop.yml is the verification. Local: make lint/docs-check/test (654 passed), make tauri-check (43 passed), make tauri-bundle + make tauri-artifacts produced MCP-Gateway-0.1.0-macos-aarch64.app.tar.gz, which unpacks with its symlinks and exec bit and passes codesign --verify --deep --strict.

title: Authorization-header-only WS auth, retire ?key=
description:
Query-param keys land in proxy and server access logs, which is where URLs get written down. Retire ?key= in favour of Authorization: Bearer only.

**Half of this is already done.** bridge.py:149 sends `Authorization: Bearer` today, and transport_ws._offered_keys already accepts it. The gateway also redacts the key from its own logs (logging_redaction.md), so the exposure this is about is other people's logs, not ours.

**The blocker is not the UI catching up -- it is that a browser cannot catch up.** The WebSocket constructor takes a URL and a subprotocol list; there is no header parameter and no plan for one. transport_ws.md:65 and webui.py already say so. Retiring ?key= therefore needs a different carrier chosen for the page, not a wait.

**Deferred on the Tauri shell.** The UI is eventually meant to run inside a Tauri app with an embedded browser, which can open the socket from Rust and send a real Authorization header -- exactly as the bridge does. Every browser-only carrier (Sec-WebSocket-Protocol smuggling, a cookie set by the gate, a short-lived single-use ticket) would then be dead code. So the decision waits for that shell rather than being guessed at now. It will also move the Origin check, since a Tauri page is not served from the gateway's own address.
acceptance_criteria: Either: the UI's socket is opened by a host that can set headers, ?key= is removed from transport_ws, rpc.js and webui.url, and a request carrying it is refused rather than ignored. Or: the Tauri plan is abandoned, in which case a browser carrier is chosen first and this bead depends on that decision.
notes:
Recorded in bd memory as ui-eventually-tauri-with-embedded-browser.
websockets 17.0.1 does support serve(select_subprotocol=...), so the subprotocol route is viable if it is ever wanted.

UPDATE (2026-09-12): the blocker is cleared. The Tauri shell landed in python-mcp-gateway-af1. Its Rust host opens both sockets with a real Authorization: Bearer header, so no browser-side carrier needs choosing -- the guess this bead was deferred to avoid never had to be made.

What remains is NOT the shell. It is that /ui is still served over HTTP to a real browser, and that page still needs ?key= because a browser cannot put a header on a navigation or on a WebSocket constructor. So retiring ?key= means first deciding what happens to the browser-hosted UI: drop /ui entirely now that the app exists, or keep it and keep the query param for it alone. That decision is the actual blocker now, and it is a product call rather than a technical one.

title: Replace the stderr port scrape with a real handshake
description:
The desktop supervisor learns the gateway's port by parsing 'listening on ws://host:port/mcp' off stderr, which makes a log line a wire format. It is pinned from both sides (tests/test_desktop_contract.py and the twinned parser in supervisor.rs) so it is safe, but it is still a coupling.

A --port-file <path> flag (write the bound port atomically, unlink on exit) or an inherited socket would remove it. Deliberately NOT done in python-mcp-gateway-af1: it is Python surface added for exactly one consumer, and the right time to decide is after the shell has proven what it actually needs.
acceptance_criteria: The shell learns the port without reading stderr, or this is closed as not worth the Python surface.
